Despite its heavy gait, the argustaur is capable of relentlessly charging down a herd of rutort and running them into the ground with 
its persistent, near inexhaustible stamina. Th e ground shakes under its weight as its hoof-like feet pound the earth. Th rough the 
evolutionary need to move quickly and yet retain a measure of armored protection, this lizard has developed segmented plating while 
its legs have lengthened and straightened to gallop over the dry and arid soil. When closing in on prey, it will extend its neck to twice 
its length in a whip-fast snapping bite, sinking its teeth into its exhausted prey. Once sated, the lizard will spend days digesting and 
building back up its energy reserves, half buried in the soil and looking nothing less than a mound of stone and dirt.

Scenting the Wind Th e argustaur has Advantage on Wisdom 
(Perception) checks that rely on smell. 
Solid Footing When pushing or pulling, the argustaur is 
considered to be one size larger, and if moved by physical means, 
it moves only half the distance, rounding up.
Ambush Predator If the argustaur is motionless at the start of 
combat, and within the Farplains or equivalent environment, it 
has Advantage on its Initiative roll. If a creature hasn’t noticed the 
argustaur move or act, that creature must succeed on an DC 16 
Intelligence (Nature) or Wisdom (Perception) check to discern the 
argustaur from the surrounding terrain.

Medium or smaller creature that the argustaur successfully hit 
with its Under Bite Attack. Failure: Th e target has the Grappled

use Under Bite on a different target. 
Hulking Stomp Melee Attack Roll: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. 
Hit: 12 (2d6 + 4) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large 
or smaller creature and the argustaur moved 20+ ft. straight 
toward the target immediately before the hit, the target has the

Th e argustaur settles into a defensive posture until the start of its

Disadvantage.
Skills Perception +4, Stealth +5
Encountering To conserve energy, this large reptile spends 
most of its time buried in the soil, waiting for prey. Only its 
yellowed teeth and red eyes visible in the mound of earth. Once 
any creature smaller than itself approaches, it will charge out in 
an explosion of soil and stone, attempting to clamp down with 
its toothed maw before the creature can evade the argustaur’s 
short but frightening burst of speed.
The jaw, with its heavy under bite and overly 
developed mandibular teeth is built for 
quick snapping bites, the bite force exceeding 
many crocodilian genus equivalents
Beady eyes rest deep within an overhanging 
brow to protect its vision against the 
abrasive grit of its natural environment
When extended, the lizard’s neck 
can reach a full four feet of length 
to lash out at unsuspecting prey or 
close the distance when in pursuit 
Hardened scales evolved into fused osteoderm plates 
to protect the lizard from most predation that can 
be found on the dry arid wastes while the toes have 
fused into hooves to run over the hard arid landscape
Nodules hang down from the creatures 
tail, used in sensing vibrations when the 
reptile rests beneath the stones and soil 
during the heat of the day in wait for prey
